sections.name: architecture

value.rationale:
CODERS, four units across two waves after a PM-authored wave-0 contract commit.

The argument is the units table itself, which is the test tenet 2 sets: four rows, each with a settled interface, each writable and TESTABLE IN ISOLATION, and each with a fence that does not overlap a sibling's. Wave 1 (u1 parsers, u3 store) share no file at all. Wave 2 (u2 adapter, u4 surface) share crates/daemon but the collision surface is engineered down to one `pub mod` line each — tenet 3.

Why not solo-pm: this is four genuinely different domains — a pure JSON walker with fixture corpora, a Postgres migration with an inverse index, a subprocess adapter with recorded envelopes, and a wire/CLI surface with eval fixtures. Each is comfortably larger than its own dispatch overhead (spawn + canary + ack + review), which is the test tenet 3 sets for whether a unit is real. Solo-pm would serialise four independent proofs behind one context.

Why two waves and not one: wave 2 consumes wave 1's actual types — u2 needs u1's parse output and u3's `DdocFileRef`; u4 needs u3's `SearchFilters` fields. Fences partition WRITE intent, not the build, so a wave-2 unit branching before wave 1 lands would be compiling against types that do not exist yet. This is a build dependency, not a fence dependency, and tenet 10 says waves must respect it.

Why wave 0 is mine and not a coder's: the shared core types are the seam every unit codes against. A coder authoring them would make three siblings wait on a contract they cannot see, and tenet 2 is explicit that interfaces are settled BEFORE fan-out. It is roughly one commit of work and it buys four independent units.

value.name: ddoc parser + discovery admission
value.paths: crates/parsers/src/ddoc.rs (new) · crates/parsers/src/discovery.rs · crates/parsers/src/lib.rs (one `pub mod` + re-export line) · crates/parsers/fixtures/ddoc/** (new) · crates/parsers/tests/** · crates/parsers/Cargo.toml · crates/testkit/arch-allowlist.toml (ONE granted row: `serde_json` under `[crates.fs3-parsers] external`) — nothing else
value.responsibility: Turn the bytes of a `*.dd.json` into an element tree whose leaves are the id-bearing rows, and make discovery admit `.dd.json` while still skipping ordinary `.json` and the generated `.dd.md`. PURE: no I/O, no process spawning, no schema resolution — the schema arrives as a parameter.
value.test_strategy: `cargo test -p fs3-parsers`. Committed fixtures under `crates/parsers/fixtures/ddoc/`, whole-tree assertions, all offline. Cases that MUST exist: (a) plain `section -> row` shape; (b) dynamic-key map shape (`done_when` -> task id -> `dw-` assertion rows) producing rows whose trail carries the key; (c) a section with no ids chunking as one Section; (d) `facts: None` taking the fallback and setting `EmbedBasis::Fallback`; (e) THE REORDER FIXTURE — the same document with its rows reversed — asserting identical row addresses AND identical `raw_hash` values, which is the direct evidence that chunk identity is (file, section, id) and that a reorder cannot re-embed the corpus; (f) a row whose `state` field is present but whose schema declares a custom vocabulary, asserting the parser records the state verbatim and does not judge it; (g) discovery: `.dd.json` admitted, `.dd.md` skipped, ordinary `.json` still `ConfigFormat`-skipped, and the admission also reached via `discover_subtree` (the watcher path). Every one of these mutation-checked: break the code, watch the named test fail, restore.
value.note: Trivial-merge point with nobody: no other unit writes in crates/parsers. You are granted ONE allowlist row (`serde_json` under `[crates.fs3-parsers] external`) plus the matching Cargo.toml dependency — that is the whole grant; any other new dependency is a stop-and-ask. HAZARD: `verdict()` (discovery.rs:712) is pure and ordered — excluded, then Unknown, then Config, then size. Your admission must land BEFORE the Config branch or `.dd.json` stays invisible and every downstream unit is testing against an empty corpus.

value.name: ddoc persistence, filters, and the inverse index
value.paths: crates/store/migrations/0014_ddoc_layer.sql (new, and the ONLY migration this plan adds) · crates/store/src/elements.rs · crates/store/src/embeddings.rs · crates/store/src/ddoc.rs (new) · crates/store/src/lib.rs (one `pub mod` + re-export line) · crates/store/tests/** — nothing else
value.responsibility: Persist and retrieve a row's ddoc metadata, make it filterable through the EXISTING filter mechanism, and own the inverse index: given a repo-relative source path, the ddoc rows that reference it.
value.test_strategy: `cargo test -p fs3-store` against the real dockerized Postgres (req 33; `docker compose up -d` first — boot reports `service "db" is not running` until you do). Cases that MUST exist: (a) an Element carrying `DdocMeta` round-trips through `upsert_element_tree` and `get_elements` byte-identically; (b) a code Element still round-trips with `ddoc` NULL — the additive change must not disturb the existing path; (c) each new filter selects the right rows and, when None, changes nothing; (d) `rows_referencing` on a corpus with NO file edges returns an EMPTY Vec and does not error — this is the pre-PR-#12 case and it is the one most likely to be written as an error by accident; (e) `rows_referencing` over a seeded file-edge fixture returns the rows, ordered stably; (f) the migration applies FORWARD on a database already holding code elements, and the widened CHECK still rejects an unknown kind. Mutation-check each.
value.note: You own migrations for this entire plan; no other unit writes SQL. No file overlap with u1. HAZARD: `search_elements`' SQL is one large query (crates/store/src/embeddings.rs:430-524) whose predicates live in the `nearest` CTE — add yours there, bound as parameters, and keep every new filter a no-op when None, because u4 will send None for all three until its own wave.

value.name: ddocs adapter — edges, schema facts, derived state, degradation
value.paths: crates/core/src/ddoc_envelope.rs (new) · crates/daemon/src/ddoc.rs (new) · crates/daemon/src/scan.rs (dispatch branch) · crates/daemon/src/runner.rs (one job-kind constant in KINDS) · crates/core/src/lib.rs + crates/daemon/src/lib.rs (one `pub mod` line each) · crates/daemon/fixtures/ddocs/** (new, recorded envelopes) · tests — nothing else
value.responsibility: Everything about ddocs that needs the world: resolve schemas, fetch the corpus edge graph, compute gate-terminal and derived state, stamp the dd version, and degrade honestly when the binary is absent. Pure parsing lives in core; only the process spawn lives in the daemon.
value.test_strategy: `cargo test -p fs3-core` and `cargo test -p fs3-daemon`. All offline, against RECORDED envelopes committed under `crates/daemon/fixtures/ddocs/`. Cases that MUST exist: (a) each `parse_*` over a real recorded envelope; (b) a recorded `graph` envelope containing `kind: "file"` edges — which dd main CANNOT yet emit, since PR #12 is open — proving the inverse index is built to receive them; (c) an unknown rel surviving `edges_for` unfiltered; (d) a `pressure` edge whose target is the literal `not-applicable`, asserted NOT to become a dangling edge, and asserted to be keyed on the rel rather than the field name; (e) `probe` against a binary path that does not exist returning `DdocTooling::absent()` with no Err, and the scan path still producing rows — the degradation proof; (f) a `degraded` envelope and an `ok`-with-empty-issues envelope, asserting health is NOT inferred from the latter; (g) `derive_state` disagreeing with a row's stored `state`, asserting the derived value wins. Mutation-check each. To record a new fixture, run the real binary once and commit the output verbatim — never hand-write an envelope you have not seen.
value.note: Shares crates/daemon with u4. Collision surface engineered to ONE line: you add `pub mod ddoc;` to the daemon module list and u4 adds its own; that is a trivial merge. You also add one job-kind string constant to `runner::KINDS` (kinds are plain strings — no migration). SNAP-IN RECIPE, not snap-in (tenet 4): ship the exact `scan.rs` dispatch branch and the exact composition wiring as a doc comment on `probe`; the PM pastes it at composition.

value.name: agent-facing surface — search, get, docs, eval fixtures
value.paths: crates/daemon/src/search.rs · crates/daemon/src/read.rs · crates/daemon/src/http.rs · crates/core/src/address.rs · crates/cli/src/main.rs · crates/cli/src/docs.rs · crates/cli/docs/ddocs.md (new) · eval/ddocs/** (new) · tests — nothing else
value.responsibility: Make an indexed ddoc row answerable to an agent: filterable in search, citable and resolvable by dd address, explained by a bundled doc page, and evidenced by eval fixtures for the three query shapes dd named highest-value.
value.test_strategy: `cargo test -p fs3-daemon -p fs3-cli`. Cases that MUST exist: (a) a search response serialising `ddoc` on a row hit and OMITTING the key entirely on a code hit (`skip_serializing_if`), so no existing consumer sees a new field; (b) each new filter round-tripping CLI flag -> query param -> `SearchFilters`, and absent flags producing None; (c) `Address::parse` accepting `plan.dd.json#acceptance_criteria/ac-0001`, REJECTING `plan.dd.json#ac-0001`, and leaving every existing `el:`/`conv:` case byte-identical; (d) `get` by dd address resolving the same row the parser produced; (e) the bundled-docs honesty test (crates/cli/tests/docs_bundle.rs) still green with the new page — it extracts `flowspace3 <verb>` mentions and compares them against real clap help, so every command you name in prose must exist; (f) the degraded shape: rels/derived None and a `next_action` naming the binary. Eval fixtures under `eval/ddocs/` for the three named shapes — "which acceptance criteria are still open", "which tasks claim this criterion", "which criteria touch this source file" — following the existing `eval/ask/scenarios/*/` layout (scenario.json with `ground_truth.search_query` and `ground_truth.addresses`). Mutation-check each.
value.note: Shares crates/daemon with u2; collision surface is one `pub mod` line each. You do NOT call the `ddocs` binary — u2 owns every subprocess call; you consume what it produced. HAZARD: `Hit` is a wire type an agent already parses, so the new field MUST be `skip_serializing_if` optional — a field that appears unconditionally is a breaking change to a shipped envelope. Tenet 6: extras-first wire fields, additive always.

Each coder gets its own worktree branching off `008-ddocs-scan` AT the wave-0 contract commit, named `../fs3-ddocs-<unit>` per backlog row 33's naming; the unit lands back onto the plan branch by PR and the PM merges — coders never merge their own. Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (~35 of 132 drained observations were shared-tree sweeps and untrustable greens) and is refused here.

What isolation does NOT remove, and what each coder must therefore respect: merge order (the PM's), ONE Postgres instance (u3's tests and the PM's integration proof share it — u3 must not assume an empty database), one observation buffer (CAPTURE with `harness observe` freely; the DRAIN is o-prime-owned and clearing it destroys siblings' live observations — list and report, never clear), and THE SHARED GLOBAL TOOLCHAIN. That last is the one with no edit-time signal: all four units read one installed `cargo` and one installed `ddocs`, so a unit upgrading either invalidates its siblings retroactively and invisibly — they stay green and become wrong. Rule: cargo 1.95.0 and ddocs 0.1.0 (node 24.7.0) are pinned in wave 0, no unit may change them, and every done receipt carries the versions it actually observed.

Fences partition write intent, not the build: a mid-flight sibling can still break your compile. A broken workspace build across a fence boundary is a PM composition concern — report it, do not fix it cross-fence.

value.steps:
Composition is an explicit, separate step, and it is WIRING, not building: everything already exists as tested parts. If a unit needs INTERNAL rework at compose time, that is a defect in the contracts phase and it gets ruled, not patched over.

Before wiring anything, ask each done coder EXPLICITLY what it ASSUMED about the composition it does not own — call order, key scoping, pre-existing store state, who runs first on a cold index. A unit can be green and mutation-checked and still carry a baked-in assumption that only surfaces at the seams; a live seat volunteering its assumptions beats the PM discovering them while wiring.

Order: (1) merge u1 then u3 onto the plan branch, `harness checks` green after each; (2) merge u2 then u4, `harness checks` green after each; (3) wire at the composition root and the scan path, pasting u2's snap-in recipe — the `scan.rs` dispatch branch that routes `is_ddoc_source(path)` to `ddoc::scan` with the resolved schema facts, the `DdocTooling` probe into `AppState::from_config` (crates/daemon/src/wiring.rs:116), and the job-kind constant into `runner::KINDS`; (4) bump `PARSER_VERSION` (crates/daemon/src/scan.rs:131) exactly once so the corpus re-parses cleanly; (5) `harness checks` green on the composed tree; (6) run the integration proof.

Composition failure modes to check DELIBERATELY, not hopefully: mis-wiring (right parts, wrong plumbing — especially the schema facts reaching the parser, since a silently-None `facts` degrades every row to the fallback embed basis and everything still looks green); interface drift from this document; envelope drift between u2's parsed edges and u3's stored refs; a per-file `links` call sneaking onto the scan path (review-blocking, and it will only show as slowness); and stale doc-comments across fence boundaries.
value.integration_proof:
Live, on this repo's own ddoc corpus, captured as the plan's exit evidence:
1. `docker compose up -d`, daemon up, `flowspace3 add .` on this worktree, wait for the queue to drain.
2. Assert the corpus admitted `docs/plans/**/*.dd.json` and `.harness/government/settings.dd.json` as ROW elements, and that no `.dd.md` contributed hits.
3. Run the three named queries live and capture the transcripts: "which acceptance criteria are still open" (gate-open filter), "which tasks claim this criterion" (inbound edges), "which criteria touch crates/parsers/src/discovery.rs" (the inverse index — expected to return empty until dd PR #12 lands, and that empty result IS the proof it does not error).
4. Take one returned address and resolve it with BOTH `flowspace3 get` and `ddocs get`, showing the same row.
5. The reorder proof, end to end: reverse the rows of one indexed `.dd.json`, rescan, and assert zero new embeddings.
6. The degradation proof: with `ddocs` off PATH, rescan and show rows still index and search still answers, with `next_action` naming the binary.
7. `harness checks` green, and the observed cargo + ddocs versions recorded.

value.when: after composition, before the PR into main
value.inputs: plan.dd.md + this impl-guide + the full branch diff. Priority order for the reviewer: (1) the plan's promises — every AC in plan.dd.md closed with evidence, not assertion; (2) composition seams — schema facts actually reaching the parser, edges actually sliced from ONE corpus graph, the inverse index empty-not-erroring; (3) interface drift — any unit that widened a wave-0 type instead of raising a ruling; (4) correctness against dd's measured semantics, which are quoted in the units table with their source: no row-in-row parser, no `file#id` short address, no name-inferred prose fields, no per-file `links` on the scan path, no health inferred from empty issues, `not-applicable` keyed on the rel; (5) contract-test gaps — specifically whether the reorder-zero-embeddings test, the stored-vs-derived disagreement test, and the missing-binary degradation test exist and were mutation-checked.

value.text: The central bet — that a ddoc row fits the existing Element/elements pipeline with one additive typed field — is unproven until wave 1. Retired by u1+u3 landing first; if it fails, the plan roughly doubles and that is a PM stop-and-ask to prime, not a coder improvisation.

Wave-2 units both live in crates/daemon. Retired by the one-`pub mod`-line collision surface and by u2 owning every subprocess call while u4 owns every wire type — if either finds itself editing the other's file, that is a design defect to report, not a merge to resolve.

The derived-state rule is a second implementation of dd's `deriveState`, which dd explicitly warned against and cannot currently expose. Retired by keeping it behind exactly one function with gate_terminal read from the schema, plus a filed ask for a `ddocs --json derive` verb naming flowspace3 as the consumer.

dd's per-verb JSON data payload is NOT frozen and moved within the last month. Retired by defensive parsing that ignores unknown fields, recorded-envelope fixtures, and keying re-derivation on the stamped `ddocs --json version`.

Silent degradation is the worst failure shape here: a None `facts` makes every row take the fallback embed basis and everything still looks green. Retired by `EmbedBasis` being carried on every row as data, asserted in tests, and surfaced in the hit — so 'we degraded' is queryable rather than invisible.
One Postgres instance is shared by u3's tests and the PM's integration proof. Retired by u3 never assuming an empty database and by the integration proof running after u3's merge, not alongside it.
